chunks: I asked Abā ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ (عليه السلام) about the saying of Allah, the Exalted:
“And know that whatever you gain from anything, then indeed one-fifth of it is for Allah, and for the Messenger, and for the near of kin.”
So Abū ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ (عليه السلام), with his elbows upon his knees, then gestured with his hand and said: “By Allah, it is the profit day by day.”
“Except that my father made his Shiʿah to be in allowance, so that they may be purified.”

key_terms.خُمُسَهُ: its one-fifth share due as khums
key_terms.ذِي الْقُرْبَى: the near of kin, referring to the entitled kin
key_terms.لِيَزْكُوا: so that they may be purified

ai.seo_question: Does the khums verse apply to daily profit and benefit, or only to war booty?
ai.summary: This narration explains the khums verse as applying not only to war gains, but also to recurring profit and benefit acquired day by day. The Imam (عليه السلام) then states that his father granted the Shiʿah dispensation regarding it, so that they may be purified.
